research_question: Among infants aged 12 months or younger, what is the effect of prophylactic skin-care interventions applied during infancy, compared with standard skin care or no skin-care intervention, on the risk of developing eczema by 1 to 3 years of age?
treatment_label: Prophylactic skin-care intervention during infancy (such as emollients, moisturizers, barrier-enhancing products, or structured skin-care regimens)
control_label: Standard/usual skin care, placebo or minimal skin care, or no skin-care intervention
outcome_description: Incident eczema (atopic dermatitis) assessed between 1 and 3 years of age, including clinician-diagnosed, validated criteria-based, or parent-reported eczema incidence or prevalence representing development of eczema after intervention initiation.
positive_direction: A positive effect size means that prophylactic skin care during infancy lowers the risk of developing eczema by 1 to 3 years of age compared with standard skin care or no intervention.
search_queries: infant emollient eczema prevention controlled trial
infancy skin care atopic dermatitis prevention experiment
baby moisturizer skin barrier eczema incidence comparison
inclusion_criteria: Original empirical studies enrolling infants aged 12 months or younger at initiation and evaluating a prophylactic skin-care intervention applied during infancy.
Studies including a standard-care, minimal-care, placebo, or no-intervention comparator and reporting eczema or atopic dermatitis occurrence at an assessment between ages 1 and 3 years.

Studies reporting quantitative data sufficient, directly or after author contact or derivation, to estimate an intervention effect on eczema development; all publication languages, settings, and publication statuses are eligible.
exclusion_criteria: Not an original empirical study, including systematic reviews, meta-analyses, editorials, opinion pieces, narrative reviews, protocols without results, and theoretical papers.
No comparison between a skin-care treatment condition and a standard-care, placebo/minimal-care, or no-intervention control condition.

No quantitative outcome data capable of producing an effect size, such as means and standard deviations, t/F-values, proportions or event counts, or odds ratios (including data unobtainable after reasonable author contact).
Completely unrelated to prophylactic skin care in infancy or to subsequent eczema/atopic dermatitis development.
moderators_to_extract: Type and components of skin-care intervention (e.g., emollient alone, barrier-enhancing formulation, bathing regimen)
Infant eczema-risk status (general population versus high familial or clinical risk)
Age at intervention initiation and intervention duration
Adherence, frequency, and amount of product application
Eczema ascertainment method and exact follow-up age
Study design, setting, and geographic region
effect_size_note: Extract eczema event counts and denominators at the eligible follow-up assessment and calculate comparative effects with direction harmonized so that positive values favor prophylactic skin care. When studies report multiple eligible assessments between ages 1 and 3 years, prespecify a single independent estimate per cohort for the primary pool (prefer the assessment closest to age 2 years, with sensitivity analyses using the earliest and latest eligible assessments). Account for clustering in cluster-randomized studies, avoid double-counting shared control groups, and use adjusted estimates when they appropriately preserve randomization or control prespecified confounding in nonrandomized studies.
